title: DELETE on an R-Tree while a read cursor is open frees nodes the cursor still holds
object: RtreeNode (488 bytes, sqlite3_malloc) in the cursor's search-point stack
lifetime_ender: the nested DELETE frees the nodes; the next sqlite3_step reads pNode->nRef in nodeRelease
reached_why: rc=0 on the nested write is the missing guard: the fixed engine returns SQLITE_LOCKED_VTAB

layer_by_arm.default: malloc (488 bytes via sqlite3_malloc, not a connection-owned lookaside object)

asan.why: RtreeNode is a plain sqlite3_malloc; only memsys5 hides it

asan.memsys5: MISSED (crashed SEGV (tool signal handler, not a detection))

2026-11-16 lab server x86-64, formal (re.notes: memsys5 hides the stale read from both tools. The read itself is silent; a pointer loaded from the stale node is then 0x2 and the program faults on the zero page. ASan's signal handler reports the SEGV (MISSED, crashed: A7.6 confirmed on the server); Memcheck reports an invalid read at address 0x2 and then SIGSEGV, which the harness records as DETECTED, but it is the same crash, not a report on the node. Default and rewrite: both tools report the read 24 bytes into the freed 496-byte node.
